ospControl.fileSystem: Programs stored as .min files, referenced by filename not O-number

modeSelectionKeys.auto: Automated operation — run programs, watch loads, distance-to-go
modeSelectionKeys.mdi: Manual Data Input — type G/M codes for specific operations
modeSelectionKeys.manual: Manual mode — jog machine, perform manual operations

uniqueFeatures.windowsBacked: Programs identified by filename (.min), O-numbers optional
uniqueFeatures.noEOBRequired: No End-of-Block semicolon needed — INPUT key adds carriage return automatically
uniqueFeatures.noPercentOrDollar: RS-232 preamble characters (%, $) not needed with USB/Ethernet
uniqueFeatures.alphanumericSequenceNames: N-numbers can use letters: NTURN, NDRILL, NTAP (letters before numbers only, e.g. NTAP1 OK, N1TAP not OK)
uniqueFeatures.clearAndDraw: CLEAR erases trace lines, DRAW restores material to solid form in 3D graphics
uniqueFeatures.midAutoManual: Special button allows jogging while in MDI mode without losing offset — critical for tool touch-off
uniqueFeatures.blankIDSetup: Spindle 1 Setup tab — define OD, length, Z-zero for 3D material simulation

programStructure.toolCallFormat: T0101 (tool 1, offset 1) — Okuma uses T + 2-digit station + 2-digit offset

G00.notes: Also cancels canned/drilling cycles. Use for positioning moves above material. CAS will block G0 moves near material.

G01.notes: Required before cutting moves. Must specify F (feedrate).

G28.notes: U0 W0 sends turret home in X and Z without going through an intermediate point

G40.notes: Must be on a G0 or G1 line

G41.notes: Tool is to the left of workpiece when looking in feed direction

G42.notes: Tool is to the right of workpiece when looking in feed direction

G50.notes: CRITICAL safety code — limits RPM in G96 mode. Must be set based on setup not machine max. Example: 2000 RPM for 2.75in stock in 3-jaw chuck

G85.notes: Multi-pass roughing cycle — specify start/end geometry, depth of cut, and the machine handles all passes. 'Canned cycle = ask the machine to do a complex process with just parameters'

G96.notes: Specifies surface feet per minute — machine auto-adjusts RPM based on tool position relative to centerline. ESSENTIAL for turning — maintains consistent cutting conditions as diameter changes

G97.notes: Fixed RPM regardless of diameter. Used for drilling, threading, cutoff. Not ideal for facing/turning where diameter changes

g96VsG97.g96Usage: Turning, facing, boring — any operation where tool moves across changing diameters
g96VsG97.g97Usage: Drilling (fixed diameter), threading (fixed pitch), tapping, cutoff
g96VsG97.g96Benefit: Machine calculates RPM = (SFM * 12) / (pi * diameter). As tool approaches center, RPM increases to maintain SFM. Prevents tool damage from slow SFM at small diameters.
g96VsG97.smaxRequired: G50 SMAX MUST be set before G96 — otherwise spindle can over-speed at small diameters
g96VsG97.smaxGuideline: Set based on SETUP maximum (workholding, balance), NOT machine maximum. 2000 RPM typical for 2.75in steel in 3-jaw chuck

turretLayout.bestPractice: Group OD (stick) tools together and ID (boring/drill) tools together, separated by empty stations
turretLayout.interferenceAvoidance: Z-axis live tools next to X-axis stick tools can interfere — place shortest Z-axis tool next to stick tools
turretLayout.charlieTip: Station 1 = roughing CNMG (almost never removed), Station 12 = cutoff blade (also rarely changed). This leaves stations 2-11 for job-specific tools.
turretLayout.grouping: Stick tools on one side of turret, ID-working tools on opposite side, maximum separation

toolOffsets.okumaFormat: T + 2-digit station + 2-digit offset (e.g., T0101 = station 1, offset 1)

noseRadiusComp.zColumn: Same nose radius value (Okuma has separate X and Z nose radius columns — put same value in both)

pValue.description: P-number tells machine how tool is oriented. Fanuc uses 'T' for same concept.

toolOffsets.whyUseNoseRadComp: Allows changing insert size (e.g., 1/64 to 1/32 nose radius) without rewriting program. Machine compensates automatically.

dualOffsetGrooveTrick.description: Use two different offsets for same groove tool — one for front edge, one for back edge
dualOffsetGrooveTrick.benefit: Gives adjustment for diameter, location, AND groove width. Without this, groove width is fixed to insert width.

CNMG.notes: 80-degree diamond insert, negative rake. Very versatile general-purpose turning insert.

DNMG.notes: Can reach 45-degree chamfers, fillets, and thread relief areas. Used for deburr pass after threading.

threadingTool.notes: 60-degree for standard threads, ACME threads use different angle

grooveTool.notes: Can step over for wider grooves using canned cycle. Use dual-offset trick for width control.

insertDrill.notes: Drills slightly under target diameter to allow finish boring. Large drills create significant tool pressure — drill ID before finishing OD to avoid dimensional distortion.

boringBar.sizing: Must be smaller than drilled hole diameter

endMill.noseRadComp: Put FULL RADIUS in nose comp column (e.g., 0.250 for 1/2in end mill in both X and Z)
endMill.pValue: P0 or P9 (both mean compensate from center tip)
endMill.notes: No CAM system compensation available when hand-programming at control

cutoffBlade.placement: Station 12 (Charlie ISM — rarely removed, always know where it is)

operationSequence.title: Charlie's 2-Axis Lathe Process Plan (from the part in class)

steps.reason: Drill while maximum material supports part — before finishing OD. Large drill creates pressure that could distort finished features.
Bring all diameters to final size
Run DNMG up face to remove threading burrs. Then redo back groove to clear burrs pushed backward.
Re-run thread tool to clean up lead after deburring
Final ID work after all OD forces are done
Part complete, separate from bar stock

operationSequence.keyPrinciple: Do most aggressive operations first (roughing, drilling) while maximum material supports the part. Do finishing operations last. Thread, then deburr, then re-thread to ensure clean threads.

materialConsiderations.stockSelection: For 2.5in final OD, use 2.75in stock — ensures concentricity and cleanup on all features
materialConsiderations.materialNotes: 1045 steel used in AOT demo, 4140 steel mentioned in 2-axis class

methods.method: Face and Calibrate (most common for Okuma)
steps: Use Mid-Auto-Manual button to jog while in MDI (keeps offset active)
Make facing cut across material face
Go to Spindle 1 Setup > Calibrate Zero
ALWAYS verify offset is still active before hitting Calibrate
Hit Reset to dump offset, move tool clear
methods.criticalWarning: Switching from MDI to Manual mode DUMPS the offset. Use Mid-Auto-Manual button instead. Always check offset is active before calibrating.

methods.notes: If tool setter calibrated with a tool whose Z offset is zero, use that tool to set work zero

workZeroSetup.okumaDatumConvention: Okuma uses the base of the part (right face/chuck face) as the Z-datum. Program zero is at the finished face of the part.

aotConversationalProgramming.fullName: Advanced One Touch (AOT) / Integrated Graphics Function (IGF)

availability.lathe: AOT-Lathe — standard on many LB models
availability.mill: AOT-Mill / IGF-Mill — becoming standard on Genos line, available as add-on for existing machines

blankSetup.maxSpindleSpeed: Set to SETUP maximum, not machine maximum
blankSetup.baseSurface: Right end for main spindle work

dimensionZeroPosition.spindle1: Not critical for program output, but controls graphics simulation. Use negative value to show face material removal.
dimensionZeroPosition.spindle2: Set to part OAL — CRITICAL: if not populated, AOT will not offer sub-spindle operations. This is where it decides to generate a full 2-spindle program.

processCreation.workflow: Touch blank row in process sheet > Process Edit > Select spindle (1 or 2) > Select operation type
processCreation.operationPerSpindle: Each new process asks which spindle — enabling automatic part transfer programming

aotConversationalProgramming.idealFor: Quick shop-floor programming, simple parts, vice jaw cutting, prototype work, shops without CAM system
aotConversationalProgramming.notIdealFor: Complex curves, surfaces, highly complex geometry — use CAM system instead
aotConversationalProgramming.graphicsSimulation: Built-in process simulation shows material removal in real-time 3D

casCollisionAvoidance.description: Virtual 3D mockup of entire machine that runs one step ahead to prevent collisions in both manual and automatic modes

setupForMill.definition: Build virtual mockup of machine, fixture, workpiece, and all tools
setupForMill.toolDefinition: Define tool assembly dimensions for each station

operation.display: Upper-right corner of screen — touch to toggle CAS display
operation.realTimeMonitoring: Shows all machine components moving in 3D during operation
operation.autoProtection: Halts program execution before collision occurs
operation.coolantNote: Especially useful when coolant obscures window — see virtual part on screen

casAndProgramming.g0Restriction: CAS does not allow G0 (rapid) moves when tool is touching/near material — use G1 feed moves to clear material before rapiding
casAndProgramming.workaround: Feed away from material at high feedrate (e.g., F500), then switch to G0 once clear

broachingOnLathe.overview: Cutting keyways on the ID of parts using the lathe turret

rotaryBroach.description: Wobble broach tool for full ID profiles
rotaryBroach.technique: Position, add slight taper at hole opening, aggressive feed rate (prevents double-clutch), let wobbling bearing do the cutting
rotaryBroach.notes: Best method if you have one

staticBroach.description: Rectangular keyway stock sharpened into a broach, held in static boring bar holder
staticBroach.toolholding: Use STATIC holder, NOT live tool holder
staticBroach.criticalWarning: NEVER use live tool holder for static broaching — axial loads without rotation will pit the bearings/races
staticBroach.clamping: Clamp very tight — significant Z+ pressure during cut

programming.simple: Call tool, M5 (spindle stop), position X to keyway depth, feed Z through part
programming.withCAxisOrientation: M19 C-axis orient to specific angle, then feed through
programming.multipleKeyways: Use C-axis indexing between keyway positions

parameters.depthOfCut: Single pass at final depth for most keyway sizes
parameters.spindleMode: M5 (stopped) — C-axis locks spindle in position

cAxisMillTurn.overview: Adding milling operations to a turned part using C-axis (spindle orientation + live tools)
partFeatures: Quarter-inch by quarter-inch holes at quadrants on OD (radial drilling)
Four 6-32 tapped holes (half-inch deep) on face
Milled hex across front of part

liveEndMill.noseComp: Full radius (0.250) in both X and Z columns, P=0 or P=9

sideActionDrill.type: X-axis drill for radial holes on OD

liveTap.type: Z-axis tap for face tapped holes

cannedCycles.liveFaceMilling: Milling cycle for face features (hex milling)
cannedCycles.liveFaceDrilling: Drilling canned cycle for face holes

cAxisVsYAxis.cAxis: Spindle rotational positioning — tool moves in X/Z while spindle rotates. Works for radial features, face drilling, hex milling.
cAxisVsYAxis.yAxis: Linear axis perpendicular to X/Z plane — enables true milling (off-center features, slots, flats). Required for eccentric features.
cAxisVsYAxis.withoutYAxis: C-axis only — good for centered face operations and radial operations at quadrant positions

machinistTipsAndTricks.tip: Always study the part print completely before starting. Write down your process list on paper — even a scratch pad works.
Do the most aggressive operations first while maximum material supports the part. Large drills create significant pressure that can deform thin features.

After threading, the thread tool rolls burrs forward and backward. Run DNMG up the face to remove forward burrs, then re-groove to remove backward burrs, then re-thread (spring pass) to clean the lead.
Keep roughing CNMG in Station 1 and cutoff in Station 12 — they almost never change between jobs. Fill job-specific tools in between.
Separate stick tools from ID-working tools on the turret with empty stations to prevent interference. Place shortest Z-axis tool next to stick tools.
For groove tools, use dual offsets (e.g., offset 4 and offset 24) for front and back edges — gives you width adjustment in addition to position and depth.
CRITICAL: Switching from MDI to Manual mode dumps the tool offset. Use the Mid-Auto-Manual button to jog while keeping offset active. Always verify offset is active before calibrating zero.
On Okuma OSP-P300, you don't need O-numbers, percent signs, or EOB semicolons. Programs are identified by filename. The INPUT key auto-generates carriage return.
Use CLEAR and DRAW at the start of every program to reset 3D graphics simulation. Not required but essential for visual verification when programming at the control.
N-sequence names can use letters on Okuma (NTURN, NDRILL, NTAP) — up to 4 characters. Letters must come before numbers (NTAP1 OK, N1TAP will error).
G96 (CSS) is essential for turning — machine auto-adjusts RPM as tool crosses diameters. Always set G50 SMAX first based on your setup (workholding, balance), not machine max.
Use G97 (constant RPM) for drilling, threading, tapping, cutoff — operations where diameter doesn't change during cut.
Okuma has separate X and Z nose radius columns. Put the SAME value in both. The P-value tells the machine tool orientation: P3=turning tool, P2=boring bar, P0/P9=end mill (center comp).
Put nose radius in the offset page rather than hardcoding compensation in the program. This way if you swap to a different nose radius insert later, just change the offset — no program edit needed.
On a roughing cut, position tool 50 thou above material diameter and run in single block first — if tool doesn't stop at that position, you know the offset is wrong BEFORE it contacts material.
CAS will not allow G0 rapid moves when tool is touching material. Feed away from material at high feedrate first, then switch to G0 once clear.
NEVER use a live tool holder for static broaching — axial loads without rotation will pit the bearings. Use a solid/static boring bar holder and clamp very tight.
In blank setup for 2-spindle AOT work, you MUST populate the spindle 2 dimension zero position (set to part OAL). If blank, AOT won't know to generate sub-spindle code.
AOT-Mill is great for quick shop-floor programming (vice jaws, prototypes, simple parts). NOT suitable for complex curves/surfaces — use CAM for those.
For facing cuts, the feedrate perpendicular to the face (across the diameter) can be relatively aggressive since it's a light cut (6 thousandths/rev typical for roughing face on steel).
If you get a good part at the end of the day, you did it right. There's always more than one correct way to process a part.

speedsAndFeeds.disclaimer: Specific S&F values from these training videos are illustrative, not production-optimized. Charlie explicitly notes 'don't hold Charlie's feet to the fire on speeds and feeds.'

generalGuidelines.roughFacingFeedRate: 0.006 in/rev typical for roughing face on steel
generalGuidelines.roughTurningDepthOfCut: Per insert manufacturer recommendations — typically 0.050-0.100 radial for CNMG in steel
generalGuidelines.smaxForSteel: 2000 RPM typical max for 2.75in steel stock in 3-jaw chuck
generalGuidelines.g96SFM: Per tool manufacturer recommendation for material — use G96 S[SFM] with G50 SMAX

okumaSpecificGcodes.CLEAR: Erase trace lines and previous material rendering in 3D graphics
okumaSpecificGcodes.DRAW: Restore material to original solid form in 3D graphics
okumaSpecificGcodes.SMAX: Maximum spindle speed setting (equivalent to G50 S[rpm])
okumaSpecificGcodes.G28_U0_W0: Home turret without intermediate positioning point
okumaSpecificGcodes.G96: Constant Surface Speed (CSS) — specify SFM, machine calculates RPM
okumaSpecificGcodes.G97: Constant RPM mode — direct RPM specification
okumaSpecificGcodes.midAutoManual: Physical button — allows jogging in MDI mode while keeping offsets active
